title: GPU link entropy retrospective and runbook draft
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact retrospective for the June 18-20 GPU instability cluster of incidents (ECC bursts, repeated NVLink link resets, and two kernel panics during driver unload). The goal: capture what we observed, surface a minimal, testable runbook for on-call, and propose short/medium-term mitigations for the Dedicated fleet and private appliance images.

Executive summary:
- Three-day window of repeating correctable ECC spikes on ~6% of nodes, often followed within minutes by NVLink negotiation flaps and then one of two failure modes: prolonged driver GPU timeouts (Xid 13) or a kernel oops/panic during an rmmod path that triggered host reboot.
- Root cause remains unclear; strongest signals point to transient link-level errors amplified by an underlying firmware timing regression on a subset of A2/RTX-class retimers. Temperature and power telemetry show correlation in ~40% of cases but not universally.
- Short-term: new on-call mitigation steps (below) reduce blast radius and buy time for lab repro. Medium-term: retimer firmware roll-forward/rollback experiment, NVLink training timeout tuning, and expanded KV/prefix cache policies to reduce load bursts.

What we saw (timeline snippets):
- 2028-06-18 03:16 UTC: first ECC surge alert on cluster-3-rack-01, correctable counts jumping 400->1200 in 90s. Automated scrub kicked in but NVLink error counters incremented concurrently.
- 2028-06-18 03:19 UTC: node n3k-rack01-gpu07 reported nvlink_negotiation timeout and bricked the lifeline; driver reported repeated Xid 43/13 before one worker process triggered a kernel panic while unloading nvidia module to isolate GPU.
- 2028-06-19: similar pattern, different nodes; intermittent high PCIe link retrain count observed.
- 2028-06-20 14:02 UTC: during maintenance, lab repro with synthetic NVLink stress reproduced link flapping only after toggling retimer power cycle and raising retimer temp ~5-7C using directed fan profile.

Key signals and artifacts we collected:
- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=timestamp,utilization.gpu,temperature.gpu,enc,dec,retired_page_count,power.draw --format=csv - showed retired pages rising after ECC bursts
- /var/log/kern.log & dmesg dumps with repeated "nvlink: link training failed" and occasional "NVRM: GPU lockup - aborting" lines
- Nvidia driver logs (nvidia-bug-report) with stacks showing driver ioctl waits and then a soft-reset attempt
- Per-node telemetry: retimer temp, PSU inlet temperature, PCIe Root Port resets counter, and retimer FW version.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Link-layer timing regression in retimer firmware: retimer firmware version X.Y.Z changes training window behavior that, under certain thermal oscillation, causes negotiation retries and ECC bursts as FIFO pointers misalign. Explains why lab reproduced only after retimer power/temp tweak.
2) Workload burst pattern + KV cache eviction: sudden long-token generations create sustained high PCIe bursts which uncover marginal silicon paths. This would explain nodes under heavy batch jobs being more likely to fail.
3) Driver-side memory reclamation bug: rmmod during a stressed GPU caused a use-after-free path that led to kernel panic in one observed case (not majority).
4) Intermittent power delivery sag on PSU causing bit flips followed by link retrain (less likely given PSU telemetry mostly stable).

Immediate runbook draft (for on-call):
1) Detect: watch for ECC_correctable_rate > 150 per minute OR nvlink_retrain_count > 5 in 60s. Alert: SEV-2.
2) Isolate: Cordon the node from scheduling (scale down or mark unsched) and enable graceful drain: redirect new inferences to warm fallback model.
3) Capture: run (as root) 
   - sudo nvidia-smi -q > /tmp/nvidia-smi-$(hostname)-$(date +%s).txt
   - sudo /usr/bin/nvidia-bug-report.sh --output-file /tmp/bugreport-$(hostname)-$(date +%s).tar.gz
   - journalctl -k --since "-10m" > /tmp/dmesg-tail.txt
   - sudo cat /sys/class/nvlink/*/training_status > /tmp/nvlink-training.txt  (if available)
   - curl -sS http://localhost:9100/metrics | grep -E "ecc|nvlink|retimer" > /tmp/prom-tail.txt
4) Short-term mitigation: set node to throttle mode (limit batch_size concurrency) and enable soft-fallback (route to model-variant-cpu if latency SLO allows). If nvlink retrain persists after 10min, escalate to infra-sre for power-cycle or retimer hard reset.
5) Escalation: if host shows kernel oops or repeated Xid 13 with driver stack: (a) collect panic logs, (b) avoid rmmod cycles; request techs to perform host reboot from BMC only after evidence capture, (c) open JIRA INC with tagging and include bugreport tarball.

Commands (copy-paste friendly):
- sudo nvidia-smi --query-accounting=pid,process_name,used_memory --format=csv - useful to find noisy jobs
- sudo grep -i nvlink /var/log/kern.log | tail -n 200
- sudo dmidecode -t 1 | egrep "Product|Serial" > /tmp/hw-id.txt
- kubectl cordon <node>; kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120

Lab repro plan (short):
- Hardware: a pair of suspect retimer boards (retimer FW X.Y.Z) + same PSU and chassis.
- Step 1: run synthetic NVLink training loop (open-source stress tool) with controlled fan profiles to vary retimer temp + run high-pcie throughput kernel (memcpy loop).
- Step 2: toggle retimer power/reset cadence to see if negotiation failure probability increases.
- Step 3: test FW rollback to prior retimer firmware (X.Y.(Z-1)) and rerun workload.
- Metrics: nvlink_retrain_count, ecc_correctable_rate, pci_reset_count, kernel oops counts.

Proposed medium-term actions:
- Expand telemetry: add retimer FW version into node inventory and alert when mixed versions present in a rack.
- Deploy a conservative NVLink training backoff on edge-compatible images (reduce negotiation aggressiveness, increase retry windows) as an A/B rollout.
- For Dedicated customers: offer opt-in retimer FW freeze until we validate newer images in lab.
- Improve driver unload handling in kernel path: instrument rmmod edge-case and add pre-checks to avoid triggering the problematic path during heavy load.

Open questions (needs owners):
- Can firmware vendor confirm change log for X.Y.Z re: training timers? (Owner: Priya)
- Is there a reproducible workload signature from production jobs? (Owner: Miguel)
- Should we throttle batch sizes by default on fleets with mixed retimer FW? (Owner: Ethan)

Next actions (short list):
- Lab run: Miguel + Ethan by 2028-06-28 to attempt FW rollback repro.
- Fleet query: add SQL query to inventory to identify nodes with retimer FW X.Y.Z and produce a rack-level heatmap (Priya, 2028-06-24).
- On-call runbook merge: copy this file into /runbooks/gpu-instability and link to alert rule (Aisha, 2028-06-23).

Notes to self: preserve raw bugreport tarballs in s3 path; avoid deleting them when nodes auto-delete on reboot. Add a small python helper to pull and annotate recent bugreports for triage.

Appendix: brief glossary
- ECC_correctable_rate: count of single-bit corrections per minute reported by vendor driver
- NVLink retrain: negotiation cycle where physical link reinitializes; repeated retrains are a symptom of marginal link conditions
- Xid 13/43: Nvidia driver error codes frequently tied to GPU timeouts or resource stalls

End of retrospective. This is a working draft — please add notes inline or drop comments in Slack #sre-gpu with the tag "link-entropy".
